reviewed_route_classes.blocking_reason: The benchmarks directly exercise whole-team current-control authority, but their management organization is authored by the benchmark rather than a canonical harness's own S3 path.

Two canonical direct S3 observations now exist, but they are heterogeneous evidence surfaces: a deterministic 54-scenario supervisor ablation versus a post-assessment crash/recovery operational regression. Their tasks, disturbance, model/provider, metrics and comparison design are not materially matched, so they cannot form a cross-harness primary cell.

The post-closure canonical admissions expose S3 current-control mechanisms, but current public result surfaces do not isolate those native paths in capability measurements. Their mechanism/performance/test evidence therefore does not add direct S3 observations.
The native orchestrator ablation changes outcome but spans both S2 and S3 mechanisms rather than isolating current-control capability.
The matched campaign holds model/tools/workload fixed but evaluates Agno and AutoGen through benchmark-selected organization paths that are not the canonical S3 paths used to establish S3 ownership.
The benchmark directly studies orchestration failures and recovery, but public evidence does not bind the measurements to native canonical harness S3 implementations.

closure_claim: Current public evidence contains three direct S3 benchmark families and two canonical native direct S3 observations: Multi-Agent Orchestration provides a controlled supervisor ablation, while Omnigent provides a first-party post-assessment descendant crash/recovery current-control observation. Their evidence surfaces are not materially matched, so no cross-harness S3 primary cell is supported. C.A.D.I.S., Awaken and ARES add native mechanism coverage but no further direct capability observation.
reopen_when: two or more canonical native or adapter-preserved direct S3 observations appear under one materially matched benchmark/model/configuration cell
an existing matched framework campaign proves that canonical S3 paths are actually active for two or more systems
a new direct orchestration benchmark binds immutable results to multiple canonical native S3 implementations under materially comparable current-control conditions
do_not_reopen_for: another whole-task orchestration score without isolated current-control attribution
another heterogeneous canonical operational-history observation that does not create a materially matched cell
another framework comparison that does not activate canonical S3 paths
microperformance or mechanism tests that do not measure a current-control intervention and subsequent organizational outcome
non_claim: This closure is not a zero S3 capability score and does not rank Multi-Agent Orchestration against Omnigent. The Omnigent row is later temporal evidence from a post-assessment descendant and must not be relabeled as behavior proven at the exact canonical assessment ref. The S3 primary remains a gap until materially matched native evidence exists across multiple canonical systems.
